shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Current inventory is balanced (1 each). Trading away A for B would just swap which good I'm short on, from 2 B to 0 A, without improving variety - I'd go from (1,1,1) to (2,0,1), which is less balanced and worse for a variety-preferring merchant.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of C, B, A. Trading away my B for A would just shift the imbalance to B (0) while A becomes 2, which doesn't improve variety. Since I value variety, I want to avoid ending up with 0 of any good. Better to keep balanced or seek trades that increase my total variety/quantity rather than swapping one 1-for-1 that leaves me at 0 of B.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Giving up my only B for 2 A would leave me with C:1, B:0, A:3 - losing variety entirely in B while overloading on A. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility despite the numeric gain in goods.
This would give me 2 B and 0 C, going from a balanced (1,1,1) bundle to an unbalanced one (0,2,1), which reduces variety and lowers my utility. Not beneficial.
This trade would give me 2C and 0B, moving from an even 1-1-1 bundle to an unbalanced one, which decreases variety and thus my utility since I value diversity across goods.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of C, B, A, so variety is balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 more C would leave me with 3 C, 0 B, 1 A - creating a large imbalance and losing a good entirely, which reduces my utility given my preference for variety.
Current inventory is 1 each of C, B, A - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and thus utility. Not beneficial.

I currently have equal quantities of C, B, and A (1 each). Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Current C:3,B:1,A:2 gives diminishing marginal value on C, so gaining B is good, but giving up 2C is too steep - I'd rather give just 1C for 1B to balance more evenly. A better trade would be giving only 1 A for 1 B, which would balance my inventory to C:1, B:1, A:1 - perfect variety. I should counter rather than accept this uneven exchange."
